chunks.arabic_text: الْخَصَائِلُ: أَبِي، عَنْ سَعْدٍ، عَنِ الْبَرْقِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ، عَنِ الْخَزَّازِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَغَيْرِهِ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامِ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Khasa'il: My father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from his father, from Safwan, from al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ: اغْدِ عَالِمًا أَوْ مُتَعَلِّمًا أَوْ أَحِبَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَلَا تَكُنْ رَابِعًا فَتَهْلِكَ بِبُغْضِهِمْ

translations.en: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Start the day either as a scholar or as a student or loving the scholars, and do not be a fourth [category] for you will perish because of your hatred towards them.

en.summary: A prophetic hadith emphasizing the importance of knowledge and the scholars. It categorizes people into three virtuous groups: scholars, students, and those who love scholars, warning that those who hate scholars will perish.
en.seo_question: What are the three categories of people regarding knowledge and scholars in Shia hadith?
